title: Gradual holdpoint allocator for session-coherent A/B tests with auto-bisect and rollback playbook
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Introduce a holdpoint allocator that enforces session-coherent A/B traffic slices, provides an automated bisect path for regressions observed during gradual promotes, and ships a documented rollback playbook for operator-driven interventions.
description: Motivation: We need safer, session-coherent A/B experiments that can expand gradually without violating user session affinity or causing noisy transients that invalidate metric comparisons. This PR implements a holdpoint allocator and an integrated auto-bisect helper that narrows down problematic traffic slices when a safety gate trips. It also bundles a human-readable rollback playbook so SREs can recover quickly. The description below covers design, how to exercise the feature, and operational guidance. Design summary: - Holdpoint allocator: allocates traffic fractions to candidate and control lanes while preserving session affinity via a lease token. Holdpoints are annotated with causal anchors (request metadata + session fingerprint) so we can deterministically replay affected slices. - Expansion policy: timeboxed gradual growth with entropy smoothing to avoid bursty jumps; supports step, linear, and sigmoid ramps. - Auto-bisect helper: when an SLO gate trips (latency or error budget), we can run an automated bisect that isolates cohorts by decreasing the holdpoint allocation and running short A/Bs across shard subsets; results are surfaced as ranked suspects. - Rollback playbook: prioritizes stepwise drain (shadow-to-control replay where possible), lease recall, and atomic traffic quiesce; includes CLI recipes and a Console runbook. Backwards compatibility: integrates with existing rollout controller; default behavior is off and must be opted in by a new rollout policy flag (holdpoint.enabled=true). Tests & validation: added unit tests for allocator maths, end-to-end simulation with synthetic traffic traces, and smoke runs against the staging rollout controller harness. Security & privacy: session lease tokens are ephemeral and rotated; no new user PII is stored. How to test locally: 1) enable feature flag in staging config, 2) create a rollout with holdpoint policy and a 5-step linear ramp, 3) trigger synthetic traffic with sticky session cookies and watch fidelity metrics in Console. Ops runbook highlights: - When a gate trips, run `redwoodctl bisect --rollout-id <id>` to produce a suspect list. - If metric delta > threshold, run `redwoodctl rollback --id <id> --strategy drain` for controlled rollback. - For emergency revert, use `redwoodctl swap --instant --id <id>` (falls back to atomic swap). Context and related work: follows on ENG-1970 (session affinity refactor) and pairs with the telemetry hooks added in ENG-2043. Commit summary: - 7 commits: allocator core, auto-bisect worker, rollout controller integration, CLI bindings, tests, docs, and gating flag. Changed areas: - pkg/rollout/allocator.go (new holdpoint allocator) - pkg/rollout/bisect_worker.go (new worker) - cmd/redwoodctl/rollback.go (new CLI helpers) - internal/telemetry/hooks.go (added holdpoint metrics) - deploy/staging/rollout_policy.yaml (example) - docs/runbooks/holdpoint_playbook.md (new runbook) - test/harness/allocator_sim_test.go (simulation tests) Review notes: This is a medium-large change but architected to be opt-in and feature-flag guarded. We focused on making the allocator deterministic and observable so operators can reason about suspect cohorts. The description string above also doubles as the top-level runbook blurb to ship with the docs.

merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash-merge after approvals. No post-merge hotfixes required; staged rollout first in staging then gradual in prod per rollout policy.
notes_for_release_engineers: This feature is behind holdpoint.enabled=false by default. Release engineers should coordinate with SRE before enabling for production traffic. When toggling the flag, use staged ramp (10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) and ensure the bisect worker is configured with the same telemetry retention as staging.
operator_playbook_snippet: If an SLO gate trips during a holdpoint promote: 1) run 'redwoodctl bisect --rollout-id <id>' and inspect top suspects; 2) if suspects point to a single variant, run 'redwoodctl rollback --id <id> --strategy drain' to minimize impact; 3) collect deterministic replay trace via 'redwoodctl export-replay --rollout-id <id> --slice <suspect>' and escalate to the on-call owner if necessary.
